newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia cenbank tightens foreign loan rules.
newsitem.headline: Colombia cenbank tightens foreign loan rules.

text.p: Colombia's central bank extended a "reserve requirement" to all foreign loans regardless of the pay- back period, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Tuesday.
Previously, individuals and institutions contracting loans abroad for less than a five-year period wewre obliged to deposit 50 percent of the value of the loan in pesos with the central bank.
From now on everyone contracting a foreign loan, regardless of the length of the period, will have to deposit 30 percent of the value of the loan in pesos with the central bank, Ocampo said.
The central bank will retain the deposit for 18 months before returning it, with no accrued interest, to the borrower.

At a press conference called to announce the measure, Ocampo said the move was designed to help the peso-dollar exchange rate. The central bank has forecast a nominal devaluation of the peso between 15 percent and 29 percent this year.
